items.q: A force of 80 N acts at 50 degrees to the horizontal. Calculate its horizontal component in N.
items.s: Fx = F cos(theta) = 80 cos 50 = 51.42 N.

items.q: A force of 250 N acts along a line whose perpendicular distance from a pivot is 1.2 m. Find its moment about the pivot in N m.
In a virtual work solution a load of 20 kN is given a virtual displacement of 0.05 m at its own point of application. Calculate the virtual work done in kJ.
items.s: Virtual work = F x delta = 20 x 0.05 = 1 kJ.

items.q: A force of 450 N is inclined at 55 degrees to the horizontal. Find its vertical component in N.
items.s: Fy = F sin(theta) = 450 sin 55 = 368.6 N.

items.q: Two forces of 40 N and 50 N act at a point with an included angle of 60 degrees. Find the magnitude of their resultant in N.
items.s: R = sqrt(F1^2 + F2^2 + 2 F1 F2 cos theta) = sqrt(40^2 + 50^2 + 2 x 40 x 50 x cos 60) = 78.1 N.

items.q: A force of 300 N is applied at the end of a spanner 0.2 m long, at 45 degrees to the handle. Find the turning moment about the nut in N m.
items.s: M = F L sin(theta) = 300 x 0.2 x sin 45 = 42.43 N m.

items.q: Two parallel forces of 80 N each, opposite in direction, are 0.3 m apart. Find the moment of the couple in N m.
items.s: Moment of couple = F x d = 80 x 0.3 = 24 N m.

items.q: A simply supported beam of span 4 m carries a point load of 40 kN at 2 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
items.s: Taking moments about the right support: RA = W (L - a)/L = 40 x (4 - 2)/4 = 20 kN.

items.q: A beam of span 10 m on simple supports carries 50 kN at 1 m from the left end and 30 kN at 8 m from the same end. Find the left reaction in kN.
items.s: Moments about the right end: RA = (W1 x1 + W2 x2)/L = (50 x 1 + 30 x 8)/10 = 29 kN.

items.q: A simply supported beam of span 6 m carries a uniformly distributed load of 20 kN/m over its whole length. Find the reaction at either support in kN.
items.s: Total load = w L = 20 x 6 = 120 kN; each reaction = w L/2 = 60 kN.

items.q: Two parallel forces of 60 N and 40 N act in the same direction at points 0.8 m apart. Find the distance of their resultant from the 60 N force in m.
A cantilever 4 m long carries a point load of 40 kN at its free end. Find the bending moment at the fixed end in kN m.
items.s: M = W x L = 40 x 4 = 160 kN m.

items.q: A cantilever 2 m long carries a uniformly distributed load of 8 kN/m over its whole length. Find the bending moment at the fixed end in kN m.
A cantilever 4 m long carries a triangular load that rises from zero at the free end to 15 kN/m at the fixed end. Find the bending moment at the fixed end in kN m.
items.s: Resultant = w L/2 acting at L/3 from the fixed end, so M = (w L/2)(L/3) = w L^2/6 = 40 kN m.

items.q: A simply supported beam of span 10 m carries a uniformly distributed load of 12 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN m.
At a pin joint two identical inclined members, each at 40 degrees to the horizontal, together support a vertical load of 24 kN hanging from the pin. Find the force in each member in kN.
items.s: Vertical equilibrium: 2 T sin(theta) = W, so T = W/(2 sin theta) = 24/(2 sin 40) = 18.67 kN.

items.q: A simply supported truss of span 10 m and depth 4 m carries a central vertical load of 60 kN. Taking a section through the middle panel, find the force in the bottom chord in kN.
items.s: Central moment = W L/4 = 150.0 kN m; bottom chord = M/h = 37.5 kN.

items.q: A block of mass 20 kg rests on a horizontal floor. The coefficient of friction between the block and the floor is 0.25. Find the least horizontal pull needed to just start it moving, in N.
A block of mass 20 kg rests on a plane inclined at 30 degrees to the horizontal, with coefficient of friction 0.35. Find the least force, parallel to the plane, needed to move it up the plane in N.
items.s: F = W(sin theta + mu cos theta) = 196.2 x (sin 30 + 0.35 cos 30) = 157.6 N.

items.q: The coefficient of friction between a granular material and the plane on which it rests is 0.4. Calculate the angle of repose in degrees.
items.s: tan(phi) = mu, so phi = arctan(0.4) = 21.8 degrees.

items.q: A uniform ladder of weight 350 N rests with its top against a smooth vertical wall and its foot on rough horizontal ground, making 70 degrees with the ground. Find the horizontal reaction at the wall in N.
items.s: Moments about the foot: W (L/2) cos theta = Nw L sin theta, so Nw = W/(2 tan theta) = 63.69 N.

Which statement correctly defines Point load?
o: a line about which a shape can be folded onto itself exactly
a single concentrated action applied at one place on a span
a push or pull that tends to change the motion or the shape of a body
the second moment divided by the distance from the neutral line to the outermost fibre
items.s: Point load: a single concentrated action applied at one place on a span. The other options describe Force, Section modulus, Axis of symmetry.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Second moment of area.
o: the internal turning effect at a section of a member under transverse load
the sum of every element of area multiplied by the square of its distance from an axis
the line through the centre of a figure about which the first moment vanishes
a framework of slender bars pinned at their ends so that each carries only axial load
items.s: Second moment of area: the sum of every element of area multiplied by the square of its distance from an axis. The other options describe Truss, Centroidal axis, Bending moment.

items.q: The statement “a procedure in which a cut is taken through part of a framework and the piece is solved as a whole” describes which of the following?
o: Method of sections
Space frame
Zero force member
Strut
items.s: Method of sections is a procedure in which a cut is taken through part of a framework and the piece is solved as a whole.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Axis of rotation?
o: a member that projects beyond one or both of the supports carrying it
the fixed line about which a turning object revolves
the internal action at a section of a member directed across its axis
an axial bar that is compressed by the load applied to the framework
items.s: Axis of rotation: the fixed line about which a turning object revolves. The other options describe Shear force, Overhanging beam, Strut.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Rectangle?
o: a member built in at one end and completely free at the other
the greatest value of resistance reached just before sliding begins
the rule that two pushes or pulls acting at a point are added by the diagonal of the figure formed on them
a plane figure with four sides and every internal corner equal to a right angle
items.s: Rectangle: a plane figure with four sides and every internal corner equal to a right angle. The other options describe Cantilever, Parallelogram law, Limiting friction.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Cantilever.
o: the internal turning effect at a section of a member under transverse load
the perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line along which a pull acts
a shape whose middle is removed so that a void runs through it
a member built in at one end and completely free at the other
items.s: Cantilever: a member built in at one end and completely free at the other. The other options describe Hollow section, Bending moment, Moment arm.

items.q: Which term is described by “the condition of an object that is at rest and has no tendency to start moving”?
o: Free body diagram
Roller support
Support reaction
Static equilibrium
items.s: Static equilibrium is the condition of an object that is at rest and has no tendency to start moving.

items.q: Which term is described by “the fixed line about which a turning object revolves”?
o: Moment arm
Principle of moments
Lever
Axis of rotation
items.s: Axis of rotation is the fixed line about which a turning object revolves.

items.q: The statement “a connection that transmits push or pull but no turning effect to the bars meeting there” describes which of the following?
o: Truss
Space frame
Zero force member
Pin joint
items.s: Pin joint is a connection that transmits push or pull but no turning effect to the bars meeting there.

items.q: Which term is described by “the sum of every element of area multiplied by the square of its distance from an axis”?
o: Section modulus
Hollow section
Second moment of area
Principal axes
items.s: Second moment of area is the sum of every element of area multiplied by the square of its distance from an axis.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Overhanging beam?
o: the fixed line about which a turning object revolves
the internal action at a section of a member directed across its axis
a member that projects beyond one or both of the supports carrying it
the direction of turning that follows the hands of a clock as the observer sees them
items.s: Overhanging beam: a member that projects beyond one or both of the supports carrying it. The other options describe Shear force, Clockwise sense, Axis of rotation.

items.q: Which term is described by “the internal turning effect at a section of a member under transverse load”?
o: Uniformly varying load
Beam
Point load
Bending moment
items.s: Bending moment is the internal turning effect at a section of a member under transverse load.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Kinetic friction.
o: the turning effect about a point, obtained as the product of a push and its lever arm
the resistance measured while one surface slides steadily over another
a procedure in which a cut is taken through part of a framework and the piece is solved as a whole
the sum of every element of area multiplied by the square of its distance from an axis
items.s: Kinetic friction: the resistance measured while one surface slides steadily over another. The other options describe Torque, Method of sections, Second moment of area.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Collinear forces.
o: pushes and pulls acting along one and the same straight line
the push or pull that a support gives back to a structure resting on it
a bearing that provides only a reaction normal to the surface on which it rests
a constant intensity of weight or pressure spread evenly along the whole span
items.s: Collinear forces: pushes and pulls acting along one and the same straight line. The other options describe Roller support, Uniformly distributed load, Support reaction.

items.q: The statement “the rule that the polar value about a pole equals the sum of the two planar values about perpendicular lines” describes which of the following?
o: Second moment of area
Perpendicular axis theorem
Hollow section
Parallel axis theorem
items.s: Perpendicular axis theorem is the rule that the polar value about a pole equals the sum of the two planar values about perpendicular lines.

items.q: The statement “a structural member that carries load mainly by bending” describes which of the following?
o: Shear force
Point load
Simply supported
Beam
items.s: Beam is a structural member that carries load mainly by bending.

items.q: Rectangle may be defined as
o: the angle whose tangent equals the ratio of limiting resistance to the normal reaction
an axial bar that is stretched by the load applied to the framework
a plane figure with four sides and every internal corner equal to a right angle
a single concentrated action applied at one place on a span
items.s: Rectangle: a plane figure with four sides and every internal corner equal to a right angle. The other options describe Tie, Angle of friction, Point load.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Tension?
o: the internal pull that stretches a bar along its own axis
a push or pull that tends to change the motion or the shape of a body
the distance at which the whole area could be concentrated without altering its second moment
the point that coincides with the centre of mass of a thin flat plate of uniform material
items.s: Tension: the internal pull that stretches a bar along its own axis. The other options describe Force, Radius of gyration, Centroid.

items.q: Which term is described by “one of two or more parts into which a single push or pull can be resolved”?
o: Force
Concurrent forces
Coplanar forces
Component
items.s: Component is one of two or more parts into which a single push or pull can be resolved.

items.q: Coefficient of friction may be defined as
o: an isolated sketch showing every applied and reactive load acting on the member of interest
the ratio between the resistance at the point of sliding and the normal reaction pressing the surfaces
the direction of turning that follows the hands of a clock as the observer sees them
an axial bar that is stretched by the load applied to the framework
items.s: Coefficient of friction: the ratio between the resistance at the point of sliding and the normal reaction pressing the surfaces. The other options describe Clockwise sense, Free body diagram, Tie.

items.q: The statement “an axial bar that is compressed by the load applied to the framework” describes which of the following?
o: Method of joints
Method of sections
Zero force member
Strut
items.s: Strut is an axial bar that is compressed by the load applied to the framework.

items.q: The statement “pushes and pulls whose lines of action all lie within one plane” describes which of the following?
o: Resultant
Collinear forces
Component
Coplanar forces
items.s: Coplanar forces is pushes and pulls whose lines of action all lie within one plane.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Rigid body.
o: the single push or pull that, added to an arrangement, leaves the body at rest
the sum of every element of area multiplied by the square of its distance from an axis
an idealised object whose shape and size are unaffected by the loads applied to it
a line about which a shape can be folded onto itself exactly
items.s: Rigid body: an idealised object whose shape and size are unaffected by the loads applied to it. The other options describe Axis of symmetry, Equilibrant, Second moment of area.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Compression.
o: the internal push that shortens a bar along its own axis
the distance at which the whole area could be concentrated without altering its second moment
the placing of a film between sliding surfaces in order to lower their resistance
the flat figure bounded by a diameter and half of the circle drawn upon it
items.s: Compression: the internal push that shortens a bar along its own axis. The other options describe Radius of gyration, Semicircle, Lubrication.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Cable?
o: a flexible member that can carry only tension along its own length
a procedure in which each pin of a framework is isolated in turn and solved for the unknown bar loads
an axial bar that is compressed by the load applied to the framework
the state in which the net push and the net turning effect on a body are both zero
items.s: Cable: a flexible member that can carry only tension along its own length. The other options describe Strut, Equilibrium, Method of joints.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Centre of gravity.
o: the internal push that shortens a bar along its own axis
the sum of area elements each multiplied by the square of the distance from a pole
the energy associated with a small imaginary displacement, used to find an unknown action at rest
the point through which the whole weight of an object acts in every orientation
items.s: Centre of gravity: the point through which the whole weight of an object acts in every orientation. The other options describe Virtual work, Compression, Polar second moment.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Centre of gravity?
o: a procedure in which a cut is taken through part of a framework and the piece is solved as a whole
the internal push that shortens a bar along its own axis
the sum of every element of area multiplied by the square of its distance from an axis
the point through which the whole weight of an object acts in every orientation
items.s: Centre of gravity: the point through which the whole weight of an object acts in every orientation. The other options describe Method of sections, Compression, Second moment of area.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Principle of virtual work.
o: a member that projects beyond one or both of the supports carrying it
an idealised object whose shape and size are unaffected by the loads applied to it
an axial bar that is compressed by the load applied to the framework
the statement that an object in balance does no total energy over any small compatible displacement
items.s: Principle of virtual work: the statement that an object in balance does no total energy over any small compatible displacement. The other options describe Rigid body, Overhanging beam, Strut.

items.q: Which term is described by “the internal push that shortens a bar along its own axis”?
o: Cable
Sag
Compression
Tension
items.s: Compression is the internal push that shortens a bar along its own axis.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Polar second moment?
o: the sum of area elements each multiplied by the square of the distance from a pole
the internal pull that stretches a bar along its own axis
a bearing that provides only a reaction normal to the surface on which it rests
an intensity that changes at a steady rate from one end of a span to the other
items.s: Polar second moment: the sum of area elements each multiplied by the square of the distance from a pole. The other options describe Uniformly varying load, Roller support, Tension.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Method of joints?
o: a push or pull that tends to change the motion or the shape of a body
pushes and pulls whose lines of action all lie within one plane
the resistance present when two surfaces in contact have not yet moved over each other
a procedure in which each pin of a framework is isolated in turn and solved for the unknown bar loads
items.s: Method of joints: a procedure in which each pin of a framework is isolated in turn and solved for the unknown bar loads. The other options describe Coplanar forces, Static friction, Force.

items.q: Which term is described by “the direction of turning that follows the hands of a clock as the observer sees them”?
o: Principle of moments
Lever
Clockwise sense
Axis of rotation
items.s: Clockwise sense is the direction of turning that follows the hands of a clock as the observer sees them.

items.q: The statement “the sum of area elements each multiplied by the square of the distance from a pole” describes which of the following?
o: Hollow section
Principal axes
Polar second moment
Second moment of area
items.s: Polar second moment is the sum of area elements each multiplied by the square of the distance from a pole.

items.q: Which term is described by “the steepest angle at which a heap of loose material stands without slipping”?
o: Angle of repose
Lubrication
Normal reaction
Angle of friction
items.s: Angle of repose is the steepest angle at which a heap of loose material stands without slipping.

items.q: Lever may be defined as
o: a pair of perpendicular lines about which the product of inertia of a shape vanishes
the condition of an object that is at rest and has no tendency to start moving
the flat figure bounded by a diameter and half of the circle drawn upon it
a rigid bar pivoted at a fixed point so that a small effort balances a large load
items.s: Lever: a rigid bar pivoted at a fixed point so that a small effort balances a large load. The other options describe Semicircle, Static equilibrium, Principal axes.

items.q: Parallelogram law may be defined as
o: the rule that two pushes or pulls acting at a point are added by the diagonal of the figure formed on them
the state in which the net push and the net turning effect on a body are both zero
an isolated sketch showing every applied and reactive load acting on the member of interest
the distance at which the whole area could be concentrated without altering its second moment
items.s: Parallelogram law: the rule that two pushes or pulls acting at a point are added by the diagonal of the figure formed on them. The other options describe Radius of gyration, Free body diagram, Equilibrium.

items.q: The statement “the fixed line about which a turning object revolves” describes which of the following?
o: Couple
Moment arm
Axis of rotation
Lever
items.s: Axis of rotation is the fixed line about which a turning object revolves.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Zero force member.
o: an intensity that changes at a steady rate from one end of a span to the other
the resistance measured while one surface slides steadily over another
a bar that carries no axial load under the stated condition of loading
the angle whose tangent equals the ratio of limiting resistance to the normal reaction
items.s: Zero force member: a bar that carries no axial load under the stated condition of loading. The other options describe Uniformly varying load, Angle of friction, Kinetic friction.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Cantilever?
o: the product of a small element of area and its perpendicular distance from a chosen axis
the point through which the whole weight of an object acts in every orientation
a member built in at one end and completely free at the other
a procedure in which each pin of a framework is isolated in turn and solved for the unknown bar loads
items.s: Cantilever: a member built in at one end and completely free at the other. The other options describe Method of joints, First moment of area, Centre of gravity.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Uniformly distributed load?
o: a constant intensity of weight or pressure spread evenly along the whole span
the second moment divided by the distance from the neutral line to the outermost fibre
the rule that two pushes or pulls acting at a point are added by the diagonal of the figure formed on them
an isolated sketch showing every applied and reactive load acting on the member of interest
items.s: Uniformly distributed load: a constant intensity of weight or pressure spread evenly along the whole span. The other options describe Section modulus, Free body diagram, Parallelogram law.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Perpendicular axis theorem.
o: a bearing that provides only a reaction normal to the surface on which it rests
the internal action at a section of a member directed across its axis
the rule that the polar value about a pole equals the sum of the two planar values about perpendicular lines
pushes and pulls whose lines of action all pass through one common point
items.s: Perpendicular axis theorem: the rule that the polar value about a pole equals the sum of the two planar values about perpendicular lines. The other options describe Concurrent forces, Shear force, Roller support.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Normal reaction.
o: the rule that the value about any line equals that about a parallel centroidal line plus area times offset squared
the sum of area elements each multiplied by the square of the distance from a pole
an idealised object whose shape and size are unaffected by the loads applied to it
the push acting perpendicular to the surfaces that are in contact
items.s: Normal reaction: the push acting perpendicular to the surfaces that are in contact. The other options describe Rigid body, Parallel axis theorem, Polar second moment.

items.q: The statement “the internal push that shortens a bar along its own axis” describes which of the following?
o: Sag
Virtual work
Compression
Cable
items.s: Compression is the internal push that shortens a bar along its own axis.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Bending moment?
o: the internal turning effect at a section of a member under transverse load
one of two or more parts into which a single push or pull can be resolved
an intensity that changes at a steady rate from one end of a span to the other
a shape whose middle is removed so that a void runs through it
items.s: Bending moment: the internal turning effect at a section of a member under transverse load. The other options describe Component, Hollow section, Uniformly varying load.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Principal axes?
o: a three dimensional framework whose bars can act in any direction
one of two or more parts into which a single push or pull can be resolved
a pair of perpendicular lines about which the product of inertia of a shape vanishes
the rule that the polar value about a pole equals the sum of the two planar values about perpendicular lines

items.q: Which of the following best describes Angle of repose?

the condition of an object that is at rest and has no tendency to start moving
pushes and pulls whose lines of action all lie within one plane
the point that coincides with the centre of mass of a thin flat plate of uniform material
items.s: Angle of repose: the steepest angle at which a heap of loose material stands without slipping. The other options describe Static equilibrium, Centroid, Coplanar forces.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Equilibrant?

the internal pull that stretches a bar along its own axis
the direction of turning that follows the hands of a clock as the observer sees them
the single push or pull that, added to an arrangement, leaves the body at rest

Shear force

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Simply supported.

a pair of equal, opposite and parallel pushes that turns a body without shifting it
resting on a support at each end, one of which is free to roll
the direction of turning that follows the hands of a clock as the observer sees them
items.s: Simply supported: resting on a support at each end, one of which is free to roll. The other options describe Couple, Principle of virtual work, Clockwise sense.

items.q: Section modulus may be defined as
o: a framework of slender bars pinned at their ends so that each carries only axial load
the second moment divided by the distance from the neutral line to the outermost fibre
the sum of area elements each multiplied by the square of the distance from a pole
a plane figure with four sides and every internal corner equal to a right angle
items.s: Section modulus: the second moment divided by the distance from the neutral line to the outermost fibre. The other options describe Rectangle, Truss, Polar second moment.

items.q: The statement “a procedure in which each pin of a framework is isolated in turn and solved for the unknown bar loads” describes which of the following?
o: Space frame
Method of joints
Method of sections
Pin joint

items.q: Which of the following best describes Sag?
o: a pair of perpendicular lines about which the product of inertia of a shape vanishes
the state in which the net push and the net turning effect on a body are both zero
the vertical drop of the lowest point of a hanging cable below the level of its supports
a procedure in which each pin of a framework is isolated in turn and solved for the unknown bar loads
items.s: Sag: the vertical drop of the lowest point of a hanging cable below the level of its supports. The other options describe Equilibrium, Principal axes, Method of joints.

items.q: The statement “a flexible member that can carry only tension along its own length” describes which of the following?

Compression
Cable
Sag

items.q: Component may be defined as

the internal pull that stretches a bar along its own axis
one of two or more parts into which a single push or pull can be resolved
an isolated sketch showing every applied and reactive load acting on the member of interest

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Second moment of area?

a connection that transmits push or pull but no turning effect to the bars meeting there
the sum of every element of area multiplied by the square of its distance from an axis
the angle whose tangent equals the ratio of limiting resistance to the normal reaction

Coplanar forces

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Parallel axis theorem.

an axial bar that is stretched by the load applied to the framework
the direction of turning that follows the hands of a clock as the observer sees them
the rule that the value about any line equals that about a parallel centroidal line plus area times offset squared
items.s: Parallel axis theorem: the rule that the value about any line equals that about a parallel centroidal line plus area times offset squared. The other options describe Tie, Clockwise sense, Beam.

items.q: The statement “the product of a small element of area and its perpendicular distance from a chosen axis” describes which of the following?

Composite area

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Pin joint?

a connection that transmits push or pull but no turning effect to the bars meeting there
the direction of turning that follows the hands of a clock as the observer sees them
pushes and pulls whose lines of action all lie within one plane

o: a connection that transmits push or pull but no turning effect to the bars meeting there
the single push or pull that, added to an arrangement, leaves the body at rest
a pair of perpendicular lines about which the product of inertia of a shape vanishes
pushes and pulls whose lines of action all lie within one plane
items.s: Equilibrant: the single push or pull that, added to an arrangement, leaves the body at rest. The other options describe Principal axes, Coplanar forces, Pin joint.

items.q: Which term is described by “the placing of a film between sliding surfaces in order to lower their resistance”?
o: Coefficient of friction
Lubrication
Static friction
Angle of friction
items.s: Lubrication is the placing of a film between sliding surfaces in order to lower their resistance.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Limiting friction.
o: the vertical drop of the lowest point of a hanging cable below the level of its supports
the fixed line about which a turning object revolves
the greatest value of resistance reached just before sliding begins
the perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line along which a pull acts
items.s: Limiting friction: the greatest value of resistance reached just before sliding begins. The other options describe Moment arm, Axis of rotation, Sag.

items.q: The statement “the single push or pull that, added to an arrangement, leaves the body at rest” describes which of the following?
o: Concurrent forces
Collinear forces
Particle
Equilibrant
items.s: Equilibrant is the single push or pull that, added to an arrangement, leaves the body at rest.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Zero force member?
o: the internal pull that stretches a bar along its own axis
a bar that carries no axial load under the stated condition of loading
the resistance that opposes relative sliding between two surfaces pressed together
an axial bar that is stretched by the load applied to the framework
items.s: Zero force member: a bar that carries no axial load under the stated condition of loading. The other options describe Tension, Friction, Tie.

items.q: Two parallel forces of 120 N each, opposite in direction, are 0.25 m apart. Find the moment of the couple in N m.
items.s: Moment of couple = F x d = 120 x 0.25 = 30 N m.

items.q: A simply supported beam of span 10 m carries a point load of 40 kN at 1.5 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
items.s: Taking moments about the right support: RA = W (L - a)/L = 40 x (10 - 1.5)/10 = 34 kN.

items.q: A simply supported beam of span 6 m carries a uniformly distributed load of 6 kN/m over its whole length. Find the reaction at either support in kN.
items.s: Total load = w L = 6 x 6 = 36 kN; each reaction = w L/2 = 18 kN.

items.q: A cantilever 1.5 m long carries a point load of 30 kN at its free end. Find the bending moment at the fixed end in kN m.
items.s: M = W x L = 30 x 1.5 = 45 kN m.

items.q: A block of mass 15 kg rests on a horizontal floor. The coefficient of friction between the block and the floor is 0.2. Find the least horizontal pull needed to just start it moving, in N.
A triangle of base 60 mm and height 72 mm stands on its base. Find the height of its centroid above the base in mm.
A rectangle 60 mm wide and 80 mm deep stands on its base. Find its second moment of area about the base in mm4.
A solid circular section has a diameter of 40 mm. Calculate its second moment of area about a diameter in mm4.
Two forces of 16 N and 4 N act at one point at right angles to each other. Find the magnitude of their resultant in N.
A force of 300 N acts at 60 degrees to the horizontal. Calculate its horizontal component in N.
items.s: Fx = F cos(theta) = 300 cos 60 = 150 N.

items.q: Two forces of 50 N and 30 N act at a point with an included angle of 60 degrees. Find the magnitude of their resultant in N.
items.s: R = sqrt(F1^2 + F2^2 + 2 F1 F2 cos theta) = sqrt(50^2 + 30^2 + 2 x 50 x 30 x cos 60) = 70 N.

items.q: A force of 250 N acts along a line whose perpendicular distance from a pivot is 0.6 m. Find its moment about the pivot in N m.
A force of 150 N is applied at the end of a spanner 0.4 m long, at 30 degrees to the handle. Find the turning moment about the nut in N m.
items.s: M = F L sin(theta) = 150 x 0.4 x sin 30 = 30 N m.

items.q: A beam of span 6 m on simple supports carries 30 kN at 2 m from the left end and 25 kN at 5 m from the same end. Find the left reaction in kN.
items.s: Moments about the right end: RA = (W1 x1 + W2 x2)/L = (30 x 2 + 25 x 5)/6 = 30.83 kN.

items.q: Two parallel forces of 20 N and 80 N act in the same direction at points 0.8 m apart. Find the distance of their resultant from the 20 N force in m.
A cantilever 3 m long carries a uniformly distributed load of 8 kN/m over its whole length. Find the bending moment at the fixed end in kN m.
A cantilever 3 m long carries a triangular load that rises from zero at the free end to 6 kN/m at the fixed end. Find the bending moment at the fixed end in kN m.
items.s: Resultant = w L/2 acting at L/3 from the fixed end, so M = (w L/2)(L/3) = w L^2/6 = 9 kN m.

items.q: A simply supported beam of span 4 m carries a uniformly distributed load of 8 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN m.
At a pin joint two identical inclined members, each at 50 degrees to the horizontal, together support a vertical load of 30 kN hanging from the pin. Find the force in each member in kN.
items.s: Vertical equilibrium: 2 T sin(theta) = W, so T = W/(2 sin theta) = 30/(2 sin 50) = 19.58 kN.

items.q: A simply supported truss of span 16 m and depth 2 m carries a central vertical load of 20 kN. Taking a section through the middle panel, find the force in the bottom chord in kN.
items.s: Central moment = W L/4 = 80.0 kN m; bottom chord = M/h = 40 kN.

items.q: A block of mass 25 kg rests on a plane inclined at 15 degrees to the horizontal, with coefficient of friction 0.4. Find the least force, parallel to the plane, needed to move it up the plane in N.
items.s: F = W(sin theta + mu cos theta) = 245.2 x (sin 15 + 0.4 cos 15) = 158.2 N.

items.q: A uniform ladder of weight 400 N rests with its top against a smooth vertical wall and its foot on rough horizontal ground, making 50 degrees with the ground. Find the horizontal reaction at the wall in N.
items.s: Moments about the foot: W (L/2) cos theta = Nw L sin theta, so Nw = W/(2 tan theta) = 167.8 N.

In a virtual work solution a load of 40 kN is given a virtual displacement of 0.15 m at its own point of application. Calculate the virtual work done in kJ.
items.s: Virtual work = F x delta = 40 x 0.15 = 6 kJ.

items.q: Two parallel forces of 60 N and 100 N act in the same direction at points 0.8 m apart. Find the distance of their resultant from the 60 N force in m.

At a pin joint two identical inclined members, each at 45 degrees to the horizontal, together support a vertical load of 40 kN hanging from the pin. Find the force in each member in kN.

items.q: A simply supported truss of span 12 m and depth 2 m carries a central vertical load of 50 kN. Taking a section through the middle panel, find the force in the bottom chord in kN.

the resistance that opposes relative sliding between two surfaces pressed together

the point that coincides with the centre of mass of a thin flat plate of uniform material
the flat figure bounded by a diameter and half of the circle drawn upon it
a figure built up from simple shapes whose totals are obtained by summation

Space frame

an isolated sketch showing every applied and reactive load acting on the member of interest
a member that projects beyond one or both of the supports carrying it

Beam

Resultant
Force

pushes and pulls whose lines of action all lie within one plane
an idealised object whose entire mass is treated as concentrated at one point
the rule that two pushes or pulls acting at a point are added by the diagonal of the figure formed on them

items.q: Choose the option that explains what Lever means.

the fixed line about which a turning object revolves
the perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line along which a pull acts
a rigid bar pivoted at a fixed point so that a small effort balances a large load
items.s: Lever: a rigid bar pivoted at a fixed point so that a small effort balances a large load. The other options describe Torque, Axis of rotation, Moment arm.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what Particle means.

an idealised object whose entire mass is treated as concentrated at one point
pushes and pulls whose lines of action all lie within one plane
the single push or pull that has the same effect on a body as a whole arrangement of them
items.s: Particle: an idealised object whose entire mass is treated as concentrated at one point. The other options describe Force, Resultant, Coplanar forces.

items.q: The best definition of Collinear forces among these is

pushes and pulls whose lines of action all lie within one plane
pushes and pulls acting along one and the same straight line
one of two or more parts into which a single push or pull can be resolved
items.s: Collinear forces: pushes and pulls acting along one and the same straight line. The other options describe Component, Particle, Coplanar forces.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what Truss means.

an axial bar that is stretched by the load applied to the framework
a connection that transmits push or pull but no turning effect to the bars meeting there
a procedure in which a cut is taken through part of a framework and the piece is solved as a whole

items.q: The best definition of Angle of friction among these is

the angle whose tangent equals the ratio of limiting resistance to the normal reaction
the resistance measured while one surface slides steadily over another
the push acting perpendicular to the surfaces that are in contact
items.s: Angle of friction: the angle whose tangent equals the ratio of limiting resistance to the normal reaction. The other options describe Coefficient of friction, Normal reaction, Kinetic friction.

items.q: Torque is best described as
o: the direction of turning that follows the hands of a clock as the observer sees them
the turning effect about a point, obtained as the product of a push and its lever arm
the perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line along which a pull acts
the rule that for balance the total turning effect one way about any point equals that the other way
items.s: Torque: the turning effect about a point, obtained as the product of a push and its lever arm. The other options describe Moment arm, Principle of moments, Clockwise sense.

items.q: Hollow section is best described as

the second moment divided by the distance from the neutral line to the outermost fibre
a plane figure with four sides and every internal corner equal to a right angle
the rule that the polar value about a pole equals the sum of the two planar values about perpendicular lines

an axial bar that is stretched by the load applied to the framework
a framework of slender bars pinned at their ends so that each carries only axial load
a bar that carries no axial load under the stated condition of loading

Point load
Shear force
Beam

an idealised object whose shape and size are unaffected by the loads applied to it
one of two or more parts into which a single push or pull can be resolved
an idealised object whose entire mass is treated as concentrated at one point

the internal pull that stretches a bar along its own axis
the internal push that shortens a bar along its own axis
the statement that an object in balance does no total energy over any small compatible displacement
items.s: Virtual work: the energy associated with a small imaginary displacement, used to find an unknown action at rest. The other options describe Principle of virtual work, Tension, Compression.

Centroid
First moment of area

Hollow section
Principal axes
Rectangle

the sum of area elements each multiplied by the square of the distance from a pole
the sum of every element of area multiplied by the square of its distance from an axis
the rule that the polar value about a pole equals the sum of the two planar values about perpendicular lines
items.s: Second moment of area: the sum of every element of area multiplied by the square of its distance from an axis. The other options describe Polar second moment, Principal axes, Perpendicular axis theorem.

Hinge support

o: the rule that the polar value about a pole equals the sum of the two planar values about perpendicular lines
a plane figure with four sides and every internal corner equal to a right angle
a pair of perpendicular lines about which the product of inertia of a shape vanishes
a shape whose middle is removed so that a void runs through it

items.q: A force of 150 N is applied at the end of a spanner 0.25 m long, at 60 degrees to the handle. Find the turning moment about the nut in N m.
items.s: M = F L sin(theta) = 150 x 0.25 x sin 60 = 32.48 N m.

items.q: Two parallel forces of 40 N and 50 N act in the same direction at points 0.8 m apart. Find the distance of their resultant from the 40 N force in m.
A cantilever 3 m long carries a uniformly distributed load of 5 kN/m over its whole length. Find the bending moment at the fixed end in kN m.
A simply supported beam of span 5 m carries a uniformly distributed load of 6 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN m.
At a pin joint two identical inclined members, each at 30 degrees to the horizontal, together support a vertical load of 40 kN hanging from the pin. Find the force in each member in kN.
items.s: Vertical equilibrium: 2 T sin(theta) = W, so T = W/(2 sin theta) = 40/(2 sin 30) = 40 kN.

items.q: The coefficient of friction between a granular material and the plane on which it rests is 0.25. Calculate the angle of repose in degrees.
items.s: tan(phi) = mu, so phi = arctan(0.25) = 14.04 degrees.

items.q: A semicircular lamina has a radius of 40 mm. Find the distance of its centroid from the diameter in mm.
A rectangular section is 80 mm wide and 60 mm deep. Calculate its second moment of area about the centroidal axis parallel to the width, in mm4.
A rectangular beam section is 100 mm wide and 120 mm deep. Calculate its section modulus in mm3.
A section of area 1200 mm2 has a second moment of area of 480000 mm4 about a centroidal axis. Calculate its radius of gyration in mm.
Two forces of 8 N and 8 N act at one point at right angles to each other. Find the magnitude of their resultant in N.
A force of 120 N acts at 50 degrees to the horizontal. Calculate its horizontal component in N.
items.s: Fx = F cos(theta) = 120 cos 50 = 77.13 N.

items.q: A force of 320 N is inclined at 35 degrees to the horizontal. Find its vertical component in N.
items.s: Fy = F sin(theta) = 320 sin 35 = 183.5 N.

items.q: A force of 120 N acts along a line whose perpendicular distance from a pivot is 1.2 m. Find its moment about the pivot in N m.
Two parallel forces of 150 N each, opposite in direction, are 0.2 m apart. Find the moment of the couple in N m.
items.s: Moment of couple = F x d = 150 x 0.2 = 30 N m.

items.q: A simply supported beam of span 10 m carries a point load of 20 kN at 1.5 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
items.s: Taking moments about the right support: RA = W (L - a)/L = 20 x (10 - 1.5)/10 = 17 kN.

items.q: A beam of span 8 m on simple supports carries 50 kN at 1 m from the left end and 20 kN at 6 m from the same end. Find the left reaction in kN.
items.s: Moments about the right end: RA = (W1 x1 + W2 x2)/L = (50 x 1 + 20 x 6)/8 = 21.25 kN.

items.q: A simply supported beam of span 3 m carries a uniformly distributed load of 10 kN/m over its whole length. Find the reaction at either support in kN.
items.s: Total load = w L = 10 x 3 = 30 kN; each reaction = w L/2 = 15 kN.

items.q: A cantilever 2.5 m long carries a point load of 20 kN at its free end. Find the bending moment at the fixed end in kN m.
items.s: M = W x L = 20 x 2.5 = 50 kN m.

items.q: A cantilever 3 m long carries a triangular load that rises from zero at the free end to 9 kN/m at the fixed end. Find the bending moment at the fixed end in kN m.
items.s: Resultant = w L/2 acting at L/3 from the fixed end, so M = (w L/2)(L/3) = w L^2/6 = 13.5 kN m.

items.q: A simply supported truss of span 8 m and depth 4 m carries a central vertical load of 60 kN. Taking a section through the middle panel, find the force in the bottom chord in kN.
items.s: Central moment = W L/4 = 120.0 kN m; bottom chord = M/h = 30 kN.

items.q: A block of mass 25 kg rests on a horizontal floor. The coefficient of friction between the block and the floor is 0.35. Find the least horizontal pull needed to just start it moving, in N.
A block of mass 15 kg rests on a plane inclined at 20 degrees to the horizontal, with coefficient of friction 0.2. Find the least force, parallel to the plane, needed to move it up the plane in N.
items.s: F = W(sin theta + mu cos theta) = 147.2 x (sin 20 + 0.2 cos 20) = 77.98 N.

items.q: A uniform ladder of weight 200 N rests with its top against a smooth vertical wall and its foot on rough horizontal ground, making 70 degrees with the ground. Find the horizontal reaction at the wall in N.
items.s: Moments about the foot: W (L/2) cos theta = Nw L sin theta, so Nw = W/(2 tan theta) = 36.4 N.

In a virtual work solution a load of 80 kN is given a virtual displacement of 0.04 m at its own point of application. Calculate the virtual work done in kJ.
items.s: Virtual work = F x delta = 80 x 0.04 = 3.2 kJ.

a pair of perpendicular lines about which the product of inertia of a shape vanishes
the sum of area elements each multiplied by the square of the distance from a pole
the rule that the polar value about a pole equals the sum of the two planar values about perpendicular lines
items.s: Perpendicular axis theorem: the rule that the polar value about a pole equals the sum of the two planar values about perpendicular lines. The other options describe Polar second moment, Hollow section, Principal axes.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the statement that an object in balance does no total energy over any small compatible displacement”
o: Principle of virtual work
Tension
Sag
Compression
items.s: Principle of virtual work is the statement that an object in balance does no total energy over any small compatible displacement.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Free body diagram?
o: the push or pull that a support gives back to a structure resting on it
a member that projects beyond one or both of the supports carrying it
the condition of an object that is at rest and has no tendency to start moving
an isolated sketch showing every applied and reactive load acting on the member of interest
items.s: Free body diagram: an isolated sketch showing every applied and reactive load acting on the member of interest. The other options describe Static equilibrium, Overhanging beam, Support reaction.

items.q: Normal reaction is best described as
o: the push acting perpendicular to the surfaces that are in contact
the greatest value of resistance reached just before sliding begins
the resistance that opposes relative sliding between two surfaces pressed together
the angle whose tangent equals the ratio of limiting resistance to the normal reaction
items.s: Normal reaction: the push acting perpendicular to the surfaces that are in contact. The other options describe Friction, Limiting friction, Angle of friction.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Resultant?
o: the rule that two pushes or pulls acting at a point are added by the diagonal of the figure formed on them
pushes and pulls whose lines of action all lie within one plane
the single push or pull that has the same effect on a body as a whole arrangement of them
an idealised object whose entire mass is treated as concentrated at one point
items.s: Resultant: the single push or pull that has the same effect on a body as a whole arrangement of them. The other options describe Particle, Coplanar forces, Parallelogram law.

items.q: Which term is described by “a single concentrated action applied at one place on a span”?
o: Point load
Bending moment
Uniformly varying load
Cantilever
items.s: Point load is a single concentrated action applied at one place on a span.

items.q: Method of joints is best described as
o: a connection that transmits push or pull but no turning effect to the bars meeting there
a bar that carries no axial load under the stated condition of loading
an axial bar that is stretched by the load applied to the framework
a procedure in which each pin of a framework is isolated in turn and solved for the unknown bar loads
items.s: Method of joints: a procedure in which each pin of a framework is isolated in turn and solved for the unknown bar loads. The other options describe Zero force member, Tie, Pin joint.

items.q: Zero force member may be defined as
o: an axial bar that is compressed by the load applied to the framework
a framework of slender bars pinned at their ends so that each carries only axial load
a procedure in which a cut is taken through part of a framework and the piece is solved as a whole
a bar that carries no axial load under the stated condition of loading
items.s: Zero force member: a bar that carries no axial load under the stated condition of loading. The other options describe Truss, Method of sections, Strut.

items.q: Which term is described by “an idealised object whose entire mass is treated as concentrated at one point”?
o: Collinear forces
Particle
Parallelogram law
Force
items.s: Particle is an idealised object whose entire mass is treated as concentrated at one point.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Component?
o: the rule that two pushes or pulls acting at a point are added by the diagonal of the figure formed on them
an idealised object whose shape and size are unaffected by the loads applied to it
a push or pull that tends to change the motion or the shape of a body
one of two or more parts into which a single push or pull can be resolved
items.s: Component: one of two or more parts into which a single push or pull can be resolved. The other options describe Parallelogram law, Rigid body, Force.

items.q: Which term is described by “the perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line along which a pull acts”?
o: Couple
Moment arm
Principle of moments
Axis of rotation
items.s: Moment arm is the perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line along which a pull acts.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Support reaction?
o: a built in end that prevents both translation and rotation of the member
the push or pull that a support gives back to a structure resting on it
a member that projects beyond one or both of the supports carrying it
a bearing that provides only a reaction normal to the surface on which it rests
items.s: Support reaction: the push or pull that a support gives back to a structure resting on it. The other options describe Overhanging beam, Roller support, Fixed support.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the single push or pull that has the same effect on a body as a whole arrangement of them”
o: Concurrent forces
Rigid body
Particle
Resultant
items.s: Resultant is the single push or pull that has the same effect on a body as a whole arrangement of them.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a single concentrated action applied at one place on a span”
o: Shear force
Bending moment
Point load
Uniformly distributed load
items.s: Point load is a single concentrated action applied at one place on a span.

items.q: Particle may be defined as
o: pushes and pulls whose lines of action all lie within one plane
an idealised object whose entire mass is treated as concentrated at one point
pushes and pulls acting along one and the same straight line
pushes and pulls whose lines of action all pass through one common point
items.s: Particle: an idealised object whose entire mass is treated as concentrated at one point. The other options describe Concurrent forces, Coplanar forces, Collinear forces.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Force?
o: the single push or pull that has the same effect on a body as a whole arrangement of them
a push or pull that tends to change the motion or the shape of a body
pushes and pulls whose lines of action all lie within one plane
pushes and pulls whose lines of action all pass through one common point
items.s: Force: a push or pull that tends to change the motion or the shape of a body. The other options describe Concurrent forces, Resultant, Coplanar forces.

items.q: Static equilibrium is best described as
o: the state in which the net push and the net turning effect on a body are both zero
a built in end that prevents both translation and rotation of the member
the condition of an object that is at rest and has no tendency to start moving
an isolated sketch showing every applied and reactive load acting on the member of interest
items.s: Static equilibrium: the condition of an object that is at rest and has no tendency to start moving. The other options describe Fixed support, Free body diagram, Equilibrium.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Tie?
o: an axial bar that is stretched by the load applied to the framework
an axial bar that is compressed by the load applied to the framework
a bar that carries no axial load under the stated condition of loading
a procedure in which a cut is taken through part of a framework and the piece is solved as a whole
items.s: Tie: an axial bar that is stretched by the load applied to the framework. The other options describe Strut, Zero force member, Method of sections.

items.q: Overhanging beam is best described as
o: an isolated sketch showing every applied and reactive load acting on the member of interest
a connection that prevents translation but allows free rotation about an axis
the condition of an object that is at rest and has no tendency to start moving
a member that projects beyond one or both of the supports carrying it
items.s: Overhanging beam: a member that projects beyond one or both of the supports carrying it. The other options describe Hinge support, Free body diagram, Static equilibrium.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Centroidal axis.
o: the line through the centre of a figure about which the first moment vanishes
a figure built up from simple shapes whose totals are obtained by summation
the point that coincides with the centre of mass of a thin flat plate of uniform material
the product of a small element of area and its perpendicular distance from a chosen axis
items.s: Centroidal axis: the line through the centre of a figure about which the first moment vanishes. The other options describe Composite area, Centroid, First moment of area.

items.q: Which of the following does NOT belong to Second moments?
o: Polar second moment
Parallel axis theorem
Second moment of area
Composite area
items.s: Every other option belongs to Second moments. “Composite area” belongs to Centroids, not Second moments.

items.q: Polar second moment may be defined as
o: the sum of area elements each multiplied by the square of the distance from a pole
the sum of every element of area multiplied by the square of its distance from an axis
the rule that the value about any line equals that about a parallel centroidal line plus area times offset squared
the second moment divided by the distance from the neutral line to the outermost fibre
items.s: Polar second moment: the sum of area elements each multiplied by the square of the distance from a pole. The other options describe Parallel axis theorem, Second moment of area, Section modulus.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Space frame.
o: an axial bar that is stretched by the load applied to the framework
a framework of slender bars pinned at their ends so that each carries only axial load
a three dimensional framework whose bars can act in any direction
an axial bar that is compressed by the load applied to the framework
items.s: Space frame: a three dimensional framework whose bars can act in any direction. The other options describe Truss, Tie, Strut.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Kinetic friction?
o: the steepest angle at which a heap of loose material stands without slipping
the resistance measured while one surface slides steadily over another
the resistance present when two surfaces in contact have not yet moved over each other
the resistance that opposes relative sliding between two surfaces pressed together
items.s: Kinetic friction: the resistance measured while one surface slides steadily over another. The other options describe Angle of repose, Static friction, Friction.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Coplanar forces.
o: pushes and pulls whose lines of action all lie within one plane
pushes and pulls whose lines of action all pass through one common point
one of two or more parts into which a single push or pull can be resolved
the rule that two pushes or pulls acting at a point are added by the diagonal of the figure formed on them
items.s: Coplanar forces: pushes and pulls whose lines of action all lie within one plane. The other options describe Parallelogram law, Component, Concurrent forces.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Static equilibrium?
o: a bearing that provides only a reaction normal to the surface on which it rests
the state in which the net push and the net turning effect on a body are both zero
an isolated sketch showing every applied and reactive load acting on the member of interest
the condition of an object that is at rest and has no tendency to start moving
items.s: Static equilibrium: the condition of an object that is at rest and has no tendency to start moving. The other options describe Equilibrium, Free body diagram, Roller support.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Hollow section?
o: the sum of every element of area multiplied by the square of its distance from an axis
a pair of perpendicular lines about which the product of inertia of a shape vanishes
a plane figure with four sides and every internal corner equal to a right angle
a shape whose middle is removed so that a void runs through it
items.s: Hollow section: a shape whose middle is removed so that a void runs through it. The other options describe Second moment of area, Rectangle, Principal axes.

items.q: Point load is best described as
o: a member built in at one end and completely free at the other
a single concentrated action applied at one place on a span
an intensity that changes at a steady rate from one end of a span to the other
the internal action at a section of a member directed across its axis
items.s: Point load: a single concentrated action applied at one place on a span. The other options describe Uniformly varying load, Cantilever, Shear force.

items.q: Bending moment is best described as
o: a structural member that carries load mainly by bending
the internal turning effect at a section of a member under transverse load
a member built in at one end and completely free at the other
a constant intensity of weight or pressure spread evenly along the whole span
items.s: Bending moment: the internal turning effect at a section of a member under transverse load. The other options describe Uniformly distributed load, Cantilever, Beam.

items.q: Which term is described by “a procedure in which each pin of a framework is isolated in turn and solved for the unknown bar loads”?
o: Tie
Pin joint
Method of joints
Truss
items.s: Method of joints is a procedure in which each pin of a framework is isolated in turn and solved for the unknown bar loads.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the distance at which the whole area could be concentrated without altering its second moment”
o: First moment of area
Semicircle
Centroid
Radius of gyration
items.s: Radius of gyration is the distance at which the whole area could be concentrated without altering its second moment.

items.q: Static equilibrium may be defined as
o: a member that projects beyond one or both of the supports carrying it
a bearing that provides only a reaction normal to the surface on which it rests
the state in which the net push and the net turning effect on a body are both zero
the condition of an object that is at rest and has no tendency to start moving
items.s: Static equilibrium: the condition of an object that is at rest and has no tendency to start moving. The other options describe Equilibrium, Overhanging beam, Roller support.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Principle of moments?
o: the fixed line about which a turning object revolves
the rule that for balance the total turning effect one way about any point equals that the other way
a pair of equal, opposite and parallel pushes that turns a body without shifting it
a rigid bar pivoted at a fixed point so that a small effort balances a large load
items.s: Principle of moments: the rule that for balance the total turning effect one way about any point equals that the other way. The other options describe Axis of rotation, Couple, Lever.

items.q: Which term is described by “a member that projects beyond one or both of the supports carrying it”?
o: Overhanging beam
Roller support
Fixed support
Free body diagram
items.s: Overhanging beam is a member that projects beyond one or both of the supports carrying it.

items.q: Which term is described by “the second moment divided by the distance from the neutral line to the outermost fibre”?

Section modulus
Perpendicular axis theorem
Parallel axis theorem
items.s: Section modulus is the second moment divided by the distance from the neutral line to the outermost fibre.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Cantilever?
o: a member built in at one end and completely free at the other
the internal turning effect at a section of a member under transverse load
an intensity that changes at a steady rate from one end of a span to the other
resting on a support at each end, one of which is free to roll
items.s: Cantilever: a member built in at one end and completely free at the other. The other options describe Simply supported, Bending moment, Uniformly varying load.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Bending moment.
o: resting on a support at each end, one of which is free to roll
an intensity that changes at a steady rate from one end of a span to the other
the internal turning effect at a section of a member under transverse load
a member built in at one end and completely free at the other
items.s: Bending moment: the internal turning effect at a section of a member under transverse load. The other options describe Simply supported, Cantilever, Uniformly varying load.

items.q: Force is best described as
o: the single push or pull that, added to an arrangement, leaves the body at rest
a push or pull that tends to change the motion or the shape of a body
pushes and pulls acting along one and the same straight line
one of two or more parts into which a single push or pull can be resolved
items.s: Force: a push or pull that tends to change the motion or the shape of a body. The other options describe Collinear forces, Equilibrant, Component.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Radius of gyration?
o: the flat figure bounded by a diameter and half of the circle drawn upon it
a figure built up from simple shapes whose totals are obtained by summation
the distance at which the whole area could be concentrated without altering its second moment
a line about which a shape can be folded onto itself exactly
items.s: Radius of gyration: the distance at which the whole area could be concentrated without altering its second moment. The other options describe Axis of symmetry, Semicircle, Composite area.

items.q: Force may be defined as
o: the single push or pull that has the same effect on a body as a whole arrangement of them
a push or pull that tends to change the motion or the shape of a body
an idealised object whose entire mass is treated as concentrated at one point
the rule that two pushes or pulls acting at a point are added by the diagonal of the figure formed on them
items.s: Force: a push or pull that tends to change the motion or the shape of a body. The other options describe Parallelogram law, Particle, Resultant.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Normal reaction?
o: the push acting perpendicular to the surfaces that are in contact
the angle whose tangent equals the ratio of limiting resistance to the normal reaction
the ratio between the resistance at the point of sliding and the normal reaction pressing the surfaces
the resistance that opposes relative sliding between two surfaces pressed together
items.s: Normal reaction: the push acting perpendicular to the surfaces that are in contact. The other options describe Coefficient of friction, Angle of friction, Friction.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Truss?
o: a procedure in which each pin of a framework is isolated in turn and solved for the unknown bar loads
an axial bar that is compressed by the load applied to the framework
a framework of slender bars pinned at their ends so that each carries only axial load
a procedure in which a cut is taken through part of a framework and the piece is solved as a whole
items.s: Truss: a framework of slender bars pinned at their ends so that each carries only axial load. The other options describe Method of joints, Strut, Method of sections.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Free body diagram.
o: a built in end that prevents both translation and rotation of the member
the push or pull that a support gives back to a structure resting on it
an isolated sketch showing every applied and reactive load acting on the member of interest
a bearing that provides only a reaction normal to the surface on which it rests
items.s: Free body diagram: an isolated sketch showing every applied and reactive load acting on the member of interest. The other options describe Roller support, Support reaction, Fixed support.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Axis of rotation.
o: the fixed line about which a turning object revolves
a pair of equal, opposite and parallel pushes that turns a body without shifting it
the turning effect about a point, obtained as the product of a push and its lever arm
the direction of turning that follows the hands of a clock as the observer sees them
items.s: Axis of rotation: the fixed line about which a turning object revolves. The other options describe Couple, Clockwise sense, Torque.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the state in which the net push and the net turning effect on a body are both zero”
o: Hinge support
Free body diagram
Fixed support
Equilibrium
items.s: Equilibrium is the state in which the net push and the net turning effect on a body are both zero.

items.q: Static friction may be defined as
o: the resistance measured while one surface slides steadily over another
the resistance present when two surfaces in contact have not yet moved over each other
the ratio between the resistance at the point of sliding and the normal reaction pressing the surfaces
the placing of a film between sliding surfaces in order to lower their resistance
items.s: Static friction: the resistance present when two surfaces in contact have not yet moved over each other. The other options describe Lubrication, Coefficient of friction, Kinetic friction.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Compression?
o: the energy associated with a small imaginary displacement, used to find an unknown action at rest
a flexible member that can carry only tension along its own length
the internal push that shortens a bar along its own axis
the statement that an object in balance does no total energy over any small compatible displacement
items.s: Compression: the internal push that shortens a bar along its own axis. The other options describe Principle of virtual work, Virtual work, Cable.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Lever.
o: the direction of turning that follows the hands of a clock as the observer sees them
the perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line along which a pull acts
a rigid bar pivoted at a fixed point so that a small effort balances a large load
the fixed line about which a turning object revolves
items.s: Lever: a rigid bar pivoted at a fixed point so that a small effort balances a large load. The other options describe Moment arm, Clockwise sense, Axis of rotation.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a member that projects beyond one or both of the supports carrying it”
o: Overhanging beam
Free body diagram
Hinge support
Roller support

items.q: Which term is described by “a member built in at one end and completely free at the other”?

Bending moment
Cantilever
Uniformly distributed load

items.q: Compression is best described as

the internal push that shortens a bar along its own axis
a flexible member that can carry only tension along its own length
the vertical drop of the lowest point of a hanging cable below the level of its supports
items.s: Compression: the internal push that shortens a bar along its own axis. The other options describe Virtual work, Cable, Sag.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the product of a small element of area and its perpendicular distance from a chosen axis”
o: Centroid
Composite area
First moment of area
Centroidal axis
items.s: First moment of area is the product of a small element of area and its perpendicular distance from a chosen axis.

Pin joint
Space frame
Zero force member

items.q: Which term is described by “a line about which a shape can be folded onto itself exactly”?
o: Radius of gyration
Composite area
Centroid
Axis of symmetry

items.q: Rigid body is best described as
