an idealised object whose entire mass is treated as concentrated at one point
one of two or more parts into which a single push or pull can be resolved
pushes and pulls whose lines of action all lie within one plane
items.s: Rigid body: an idealised object whose shape and size are unaffected by the loads applied to it. The other options describe Coplanar forces, Component, Particle.

items.q: Which of the following does NOT belong to Friction?
o: Coefficient of friction
Limiting friction
Principle of virtual work
Friction
items.s: Every other option belongs to Friction. “Principle of virtual work” belongs to Cables and virtual work, not Friction.

items.q: Hinge support may be defined as
o: a member that projects beyond one or both of the supports carrying it
a connection that prevents translation but allows free rotation about an axis
the state in which the net push and the net turning effect on a body are both zero
the condition of an object that is at rest and has no tendency to start moving
items.s: Hinge support: a connection that prevents translation but allows free rotation about an axis. The other options describe Static equilibrium, Overhanging beam, Equilibrium.

items.q: Which term is described by “a plane figure with four sides and every internal corner equal to a right angle”?
o: Parallel axis theorem
Principal axes
Rectangle
Section modulus
items.s: Rectangle is a plane figure with four sides and every internal corner equal to a right angle.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Hollow section?
o: a pair of perpendicular lines about which the product of inertia of a shape vanishes
a shape whose middle is removed so that a void runs through it
a plane figure with four sides and every internal corner equal to a right angle
the rule that the value about any line equals that about a parallel centroidal line plus area times offset squared
items.s: Hollow section: a shape whose middle is removed so that a void runs through it. The other options describe Principal axes, Parallel axis theorem, Rectangle.

items.q: A simply supported truss of span 16 m and depth 3 m carries a central vertical load of 40 kN. Taking a section through the middle panel, find the force in the bottom chord in kN.
items.s: Central moment = W L/4 = 160.0 kN m; bottom chord = M/h = 53.33 kN.

items.q: A block of mass 12 kg rests on a plane inclined at 15 degrees to the horizontal, with coefficient of friction 0.3. Find the least force, parallel to the plane, needed to move it up the plane in N.
items.s: F = W(sin theta + mu cos theta) = 117.7 x (sin 15 + 0.3 cos 15) = 64.58 N.

items.q: A composite area consists of part A of area 900 mm2 whose centroid lies 30 mm above a base line and part B of area 700 mm2 whose centroid lies 65 mm above the same line. Find the height of the centroid of the whole area above the base in mm.
A section of area 1200 mm2 has a second moment of area of 2400000 mm4 about its own centroidal axis. Find its second moment of area about a parallel axis 40 mm away, in mm4.
A cable of span 12 m carries a uniformly distributed load of 2.5 kN/m along the horizontal and sags 2.5 m at midspan. Find the horizontal component of the tension in kN.
Two forces of 24 N and 21 N act at one point at right angles to each other. Find the magnitude of their resultant in N.
A force of 300 N acts at 20 degrees to the horizontal. Calculate its horizontal component in N.
items.s: Fx = F cos(theta) = 300 cos 20 = 281.9 N.

items.q: A force of 450 N is inclined at 35 degrees to the horizontal. Find its vertical component in N.
items.s: Fy = F sin(theta) = 450 sin 35 = 258.1 N.

items.q: Two forces of 80 N and 60 N act at a point with an included angle of 60 degrees. Find the magnitude of their resultant in N.
items.s: R = sqrt(F1^2 + F2^2 + 2 F1 F2 cos theta) = sqrt(80^2 + 60^2 + 2 x 80 x 60 x cos 60) = 121.7 N.

items.q: A force of 40 N acts along a line whose perpendicular distance from a pivot is 0.8 m. Find its moment about the pivot in N m.
A force of 150 N is applied at the end of a spanner 0.5 m long, at 60 degrees to the handle. Find the turning moment about the nut in N m.
items.s: M = F L sin(theta) = 150 x 0.5 x sin 60 = 64.95 N m.

items.q: Two parallel forces of 50 N each, opposite in direction, are 0.2 m apart. Find the moment of the couple in N m.
items.s: Moment of couple = F x d = 50 x 0.2 = 10 N m.

items.q: A simply supported beam of span 10 m carries a point load of 50 kN at 2.5 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
items.s: Taking moments about the right support: RA = W (L - a)/L = 50 x (10 - 2.5)/10 = 37.5 kN.

items.q: A simply supported beam of span 3 m carries a uniformly distributed load of 8 kN/m over its whole length. Find the reaction at either support in kN.
items.s: Total load = w L = 8 x 3 = 24 kN; each reaction = w L/2 = 12 kN.

items.q: Two parallel forces of 30 N and 60 N act in the same direction at points 0.6 m apart. Find the distance of their resultant from the 30 N force in m.
A cantilever 2.5 m long carries a uniformly distributed load of 6 kN/m over its whole length. Find the bending moment at the fixed end in kN m.
A simply supported beam of span 5 m carries a uniformly distributed load of 8 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN m.
At a pin joint two identical inclined members, each at 60 degrees to the horizontal, together support a vertical load of 20 kN hanging from the pin. Find the force in each member in kN.
items.s: Vertical equilibrium: 2 T sin(theta) = W, so T = W/(2 sin theta) = 20/(2 sin 60) = 11.55 kN.

items.q: A block of mass 20 kg rests on a horizontal floor. The coefficient of friction between the block and the floor is 0.4. Find the least horizontal pull needed to just start it moving, in N.
The coefficient of friction between a granular material and the plane on which it rests is 0.45. Calculate the angle of repose in degrees.
items.s: tan(phi) = mu, so phi = arctan(0.45) = 24.23 degrees.

items.q: A rectangular section is 80 mm wide and 120 mm deep. Calculate its second moment of area about the centroidal axis parallel to the width, in mm4.
A rectangular beam section is 80 mm wide and 80 mm deep. Calculate its section modulus in mm3.
A section of area 2000 mm2 has a second moment of area of 450000 mm4 about a centroidal axis. Calculate its radius of gyration in mm.
In a virtual work solution a load of 20 kN is given a virtual displacement of 0.15 m at its own point of application. Calculate the virtual work done in kJ.
items.s: Virtual work = F x delta = 20 x 0.15 = 3 kJ.

items.q: A beam of span 10 m on simple supports carries 20 kN at 2 m from the left end and 25 kN at 7 m from the same end. Find the left reaction in kN.
items.s: Moments about the right end: RA = (W1 x1 + W2 x2)/L = (20 x 2 + 25 x 7)/10 = 21.5 kN.

items.q: A cantilever 5 m long carries a triangular load that rises from zero at the free end to 18 kN/m at the fixed end. Find the bending moment at the fixed end in kN m.
items.s: Resultant = w L/2 acting at L/3 from the fixed end, so M = (w L/2)(L/3) = w L^2/6 = 75 kN m.

items.q: A simply supported truss of span 16 m and depth 3 m carries a central vertical load of 50 kN. Taking a section through the middle panel, find the force in the bottom chord in kN.
items.s: Central moment = W L/4 = 200.0 kN m; bottom chord = M/h = 66.67 kN.

items.q: A block of mass 12 kg rests on a plane inclined at 20 degrees to the horizontal, with coefficient of friction 0.4. Find the least force, parallel to the plane, needed to move it up the plane in N.
items.s: F = W(sin theta + mu cos theta) = 117.7 x (sin 20 + 0.4 cos 20) = 84.51 N.

items.q: A composite area consists of part A of area 900 mm2 whose centroid lies 40 mm above a base line and part B of area 500 mm2 whose centroid lies 60 mm above the same line. Find the height of the centroid of the whole area above the base in mm.
A section of area 1000 mm2 has a second moment of area of 1600000 mm4 about its own centroidal axis. Find its second moment of area about a parallel axis 50 mm away, in mm4.
A hollow circular section has an outside diameter of 80 mm and an inside diameter of 60 mm. Find its second moment of area about a diameter in mm4.
A cable of span 16 m carries a uniformly distributed load of 4 kN/m along the horizontal and sags 3 m at midspan. Find the horizontal component of the tension in kN.
Two forces of 12 N and 20 N act at one point at right angles to each other. Find the magnitude of their resultant in N.
A force of 240 N is inclined at 15 degrees to the horizontal. Find its vertical component in N.
items.s: Fy = F sin(theta) = 240 sin 15 = 62.12 N.

items.q: Two forces of 30 N and 40 N act at a point with an included angle of 75 degrees. Find the magnitude of their resultant in N.
items.s: R = sqrt(F1^2 + F2^2 + 2 F1 F2 cos theta) = sqrt(30^2 + 40^2 + 2 x 30 x 40 x cos 75) = 55.87 N.

items.q: A force of 120 N acts along a line whose perpendicular distance from a pivot is 0.25 m. Find its moment about the pivot in N m.
A force of 100 N is applied at the end of a spanner 0.25 m long, at 40 degrees to the handle. Find the turning moment about the nut in N m.
items.s: M = F L sin(theta) = 100 x 0.25 x sin 40 = 16.07 N m.

items.q: Two parallel forces of 120 N each, opposite in direction, are 0.4 m apart. Find the moment of the couple in N m.
items.s: Moment of couple = F x d = 120 x 0.4 = 48 N m.

items.q: A simply supported beam of span 6 m carries a point load of 20 kN at 1.5 m from the left support. Find the left reaction in kN.
items.s: Taking moments about the right support: RA = W (L - a)/L = 20 x (6 - 1.5)/6 = 15 kN.

items.q: A simply supported beam of span 3 m carries a uniformly distributed load of 15 kN/m over its whole length. Find the reaction at either support in kN.
items.s: Total load = w L = 15 x 3 = 45 kN; each reaction = w L/2 = 22.5 kN.

items.q: Two parallel forces of 20 N and 40 N act in the same direction at points 1.2 m apart. Find the distance of their resultant from the 20 N force in m.
A cantilever 4 m long carries a point load of 20 kN at its free end. Find the bending moment at the fixed end in kN m.
items.s: M = W x L = 20 x 4 = 80 kN m.

items.q: A cantilever 2.5 m long carries a uniformly distributed load of 8 kN/m over its whole length. Find the bending moment at the fixed end in kN m.
A simply supported beam of span 8 m carries a uniformly distributed load of 12 kN/m. Find the maximum bending moment in kN m.
A block of mass 50 kg rests on a horizontal floor. The coefficient of friction between the block and the floor is 0.2. Find the least horizontal pull needed to just start it moving, in N.
A triangle of base 72 mm and height 120 mm stands on its base. Find the height of its centroid above the base in mm.
A rectangular section is 50 mm wide and 120 mm deep. Calculate its second moment of area about the centroidal axis parallel to the width, in mm4.
A rectangular beam section is 60 mm wide and 80 mm deep. Calculate its section modulus in mm3.
A section of area 2000 mm2 has a second moment of area of 288000 mm4 about a centroidal axis. Calculate its radius of gyration in mm.
In a virtual work solution a load of 30 kN is given a virtual displacement of 0.04 m at its own point of application. Calculate the virtual work done in kJ.
items.s: Virtual work = F x delta = 30 x 0.04 = 1.2 kJ.

items.q: A beam of span 6 m on simple supports carries 50 kN at 2 m from the left end and 30 kN at 5 m from the same end. Find the left reaction in kN.
items.s: Moments about the right end: RA = (W1 x1 + W2 x2)/L = (50 x 2 + 30 x 5)/6 = 41.67 kN.

items.q: A simply supported truss of span 12 m and depth 4 m carries a central vertical load of 20 kN. Taking a section through the middle panel, find the force in the bottom chord in kN.
items.s: Central moment = W L/4 = 60.0 kN m; bottom chord = M/h = 15 kN.

items.q: A block of mass 20 kg rests on a plane inclined at 10 degrees to the horizontal, with coefficient of friction 0.3. Find the least force, parallel to the plane, needed to move it up the plane in N.
items.s: F = W(sin theta + mu cos theta) = 196.2 x (sin 10 + 0.3 cos 10) = 92.04 N.

items.q: A composite area consists of part A of area 600 mm2 whose centroid lies 35 mm above a base line and part B of area 300 mm2 whose centroid lies 65 mm above the same line. Find the height of the centroid of the whole area above the base in mm.

items.s: Fx = F cos(theta) = 250 cos 35 = 204.8 N.

items.q: Two forces of 50 N and 30 N act at a point with an included angle of 120 degrees. Find the magnitude of their resultant in N.
items.s: R = sqrt(F1^2 + F2^2 + 2 F1 F2 cos theta) = sqrt(50^2 + 30^2 + 2 x 50 x 30 x cos 120) = 43.59 N.

items.q: A force of 200 N acts along a line whose perpendicular distance from a pivot is 0.3 m. Find its moment about the pivot in N m.
A force of 100 N is applied at the end of a spanner 0.5 m long, at 30 degrees to the handle. Find the turning moment about the nut in N m.

items.q: In this course, Kinetic friction refers to
o: the angle whose tangent equals the ratio of limiting resistance to the normal reaction
the placing of a film between sliding surfaces in order to lower their resistance
the ratio between the resistance at the point of sliding and the normal reaction pressing the surfaces
the resistance measured while one surface slides steadily over another
items.s: Kinetic friction: the resistance measured while one surface slides steadily over another. The other options describe Lubrication, Coefficient of friction, Angle of friction.

items.q: The correct meaning of Friction is
o: the steepest angle at which a heap of loose material stands without slipping
the resistance that opposes relative sliding between two surfaces pressed together
the resistance present when two surfaces in contact have not yet moved over each other
the resistance measured while one surface slides steadily over another
items.s: Friction: the resistance that opposes relative sliding between two surfaces pressed together. The other options describe Static friction, Kinetic friction, Angle of repose.

items.q: Second moment of area may be defined as
o: the sum of every element of area multiplied by the square of its distance from an axis
a shape whose middle is removed so that a void runs through it
a plane figure with four sides and every internal corner equal to a right angle
a pair of perpendicular lines about which the product of inertia of a shape vanishes
items.s: Second moment of area: the sum of every element of area multiplied by the square of its distance from an axis. The other options describe Hollow section, Principal axes, Rectangle.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Polar second moment.
o: the rule that the polar value about a pole equals the sum of the two planar values about perpendicular lines
the sum of every element of area multiplied by the square of its distance from an axis
the sum of area elements each multiplied by the square of the distance from a pole
a pair of perpendicular lines about which the product of inertia of a shape vanishes
items.s: Polar second moment: the sum of area elements each multiplied by the square of the distance from a pole. The other options describe Perpendicular axis theorem, Principal axes, Second moment of area.
